status: PRE-REGISTERED 2026-09-24, before any P2 array was submitted. Frozen at commit time; revise only by adding a dated amendment block, never by editing this one.
task: spec v3 SS.P2 -- held-out link prediction: for every held-out LEAF node whose parent edge was withheld (Tasks 1-2), rank its true parent among its grandparent's other children (Task 4's candidate_pool, strategy='grandparent_children') using the trained embedding, at metazoa scale. Answers whether the geometry predicts taxonomic relations it never trained on, or only memorises the training closure -- Burkhard's objection to Figure 4.
why: Two prior gates in this project failed for two DIFFERENT wrong reasons on the SAME mistake: Task 9's frozen gate (b) could not distinguish a CONVERGED arm from a NEVER-TRAINED one (flat final-phase loss means both); amendment 2 fixed that and was then blind to Task 8's fixed arm, whose loss ROSE 3.90->4.02 while its S_angle simultaneously ROSE 0.892->0.933 -- the model improved throughout even though the proxy said otherwise. The common cause is that training loss is a proxy for the quantity of interest, and here the two arms' losses are not even the same quantity (vis00 vs vis50 take different numbers of optimizer steps per epoch; RandomDAG trains against a different closure entirely). P2 therefore has NO training-loss gate at all -- see validity_gate below for the replacement design and the reasoning stated in the artifact itself, not just in this session's prose.

arms.vis00: vis00_s{0,1,2} -- Task 2 visibility=0% split, metazoa_33208_clean scale; LRZ tags p2_vis00_s{0,1,2} (Task 8). Trained and scored against the REAL taxonomy closure.
arms.vis50: vis50_s{0,1,2} -- Task 2 visibility=50% split, same scale; LRZ tags p2_vis50_s{0,1,2}. Trained and scored against the REAL taxonomy closure.
arms.randomdag: randomdag_s{0,1,2} -- USER-approved 2026-09-24, the third arm of a single 9-element array, declared HERE and now, before any arm's numbers exist. Built from src/taxembed/eval/randomdag.py::randomize_parents(parent, depth, seed): every non-root node keeps its own DEPTH exactly but is rewired to a uniformly random parent at depth-1, so the closure's pair count (= sum of depth over all nodes) is preserved exactly, not approximately. The arm holds out parent edges from the RANDOMISED tree and is scored against the RANDOMISED parents -- its own held-out node set and candidate pools are built from the randomised closure, not the real one. It asks whether the model does as well on a scrambled taxonomy as on the real one: if it does, the geometry is memorising tree SHAPE (depth, branching pattern), not taxonomy. Because pool sizes (grandparent fan-out) are not preserved by the rewiring, this arm's own baselines.sibling_chance_mean can differ numerically from the real-tree arms' -- read it from this arm's own scoring run (recorded under 'baselines_randomdag' in the merged Task 6 JSON when it differs from 'baselines'; p2_verdict falls back to the shared 'baselines' block when a dedicated one is not present, and that fallback is stated explicitly in the code so it cannot pass as a hidden assumption).
arms.scale: metazoa_33208_clean (498,246 nodes) -- Task 8/9's scale; RandomDAG rewires this same node set's parent assignments so node identities line up 1:1 with the real-tree arms.

declared_confounds: Visibility 0% trains on far fewer retained pairs than visibility 50%, so the two arms take very different numbers of optimizer steps per epoch. vis00 vs vis50 is NOT a controlled contrast on compute; any comparison between them is descriptive, never a causal claim about the visibility knob alone.

The candidate pool is the grandparent's children, so pool size varies from 2 to tens of thousands across held-out nodes. mean_rank is therefore NOT comparable across strata or across arms with different pool-size distributions (vis00/vis50 vs randomdag, whose rewiring changes fan-out); normalized_rank ((rank-1)/(pool-1)) is the comparable quantity.

Held-out leaves are, by construction, the SHALLOWEST leaves in the eligible band: deeper leaves fall outside the declared depth window [11, 28] (Task 1/2) and are never candidates for holdout. Any generalisation claim is scoped to that depth band, not to the full tree.

Held-out nodes are EXEMPT from visibility thinning (Task 2), so at every visibility setting they retain exactly depth-1 ancestry rows -- more of their own ancestry than a random RETAINED node does at visibility 0.5, where retained nodes are thinned. This exemption is deliberate, not an oversight: without it, held-out nodes would appear in zero training rows at visibility 0.0 and would carry untrained embeddings, making the floor gate meaningless at that visibility. It does mean vis00 and vis50 are not comparable on 'how much ancestry did the held-out node see during training' -- that quantity is held out of the thinning by design at both settings.

metrics.primary: MRR (src/taxembed/eval/linkpred.py::linkpred_metrics) on the held-out TEST nodes at the final checkpoint (epoch 200), per run, using COSINE distance (scripts/score_p2_linkpred.py --metric cosine, the checkpoint's un-suffixed 'metrics' key). Per-run value = mean MRR over the trailing rolling window of scored checkpoints nearest epoch 200 (mirrors the S_angle rolling-window convention in results/recipe_angular_comparison.json and results/objective_integrity_delta_preregistration.json); within-run jitter reported as that window's SD.
metrics.primary_reason: The candidate pool is the grandparent's children -- all candidates share the query's grandparent and therefore the SAME target radius (this project established the radius is PLANTED: initialised at the depth's target value and regularised back to it). A depth-homogeneous pool means the planted radius cannot discriminate among candidates AT ALL; ranking on it would be chance. The ranking is angular structure alone, by construction of the pool -- which is exactly the answer to the objection that the headline metric is planted. Poincare distance is still computed and stored as a secondary metric on the identical pools (metrics_poincare), so the choice can be revisited in analysis without re-running anything.
secondary: mean_rank, hits_at_1, hits_at_10, normalized_rank under both cosine and Poincare distance (metrics_cosine / metrics_poincare)
baselines.sibling_chance_mean, baselines.vendrov_recall (expected 0.0 by construction -- the held-out edge is the one edge no visible closure can supply), baselines.majority_parent_rate
per-checkpoint training loss (trainer.loss) and reg_loss -- RECORDED for every scored checkpoint as a descriptive trajectory, NEVER used to gate or read a verdict; see validity_gate

validity_gate: P2 HAS NO TRAINING-LOSS GATE (ruled 2026-09-24, after two prior gate failures on the training-loss proxy -- see 'why'). Three gates, all operating on the metric of interest or on a fact about the run, never on loss: (a) LEARNING GATE -- max_t MRR(t) - MRR(init) > 10 x within-run jitter SD, where MRR(t) is the run's own primary-metric trajectory and MRR(init) is the primary metric at that run's earliest scored checkpoint (P2's scorer records no separate untrained-embedding baseline the way S_angle's init_null does, so the run's own first checkpoint stands in for it). This measures the quantity of interest directly rather than a proxy for it, and a zero or non-finite jitter SD FAILS the gate outright rather than trivially passing it (a degenerate zero-variance fixture must never collapse the 10x threshold to zero and let any rise through -- that exact bug shipped once already in this project's test suite). (b) FLOOR GATE -- an arm-seed whose per-run MRR does not exceed baselines.sibling_chance_mean is UNINFORMATIVE, not a result: a model at chance has said nothing about generalisation, whatever its loss did. (c) COMPLETION CHECK -- the declared final checkpoint (epoch 200) must exist among the scored checkpoints. This is a FACT about the run (a file either exists and was scored, or it does not), not an inference about training dynamics, so unlike a loss-shape gate it cannot misread a converged run as diverged or vice versa. Any of (a)/(b)/(c) failing for ANY seed of ANY arm (including the RandomDAG control) makes the WHOLE verdict UNINFORMATIVE, never a directional read in either direction -- same precedence as the Task 8/9 engine. Training loss per checkpoint is still recorded in full (see metrics.secondary) so a reader can look at it, but it is deliberately absent from every gate; that omission is the fix, not an oversight, and this sentence is the record of the reasoning so a future editor cannot quietly reintroduce a loss gate.

readings.GENERALISES: For a real-tree arm (vis00 or vis50): all 3 seeds' per-run MRR exceed baselines.sibling_chance_mean by >= 2x that arm's pooled within-arm seed SD (a margin condition, checked on the minimum seed so a single weak seed cannot be averaged away), AND all 3 seeds' MRR exceed all 3 of the RandomDAG arm's seeds' MRR (all-above-all, mirroring the Task 8/9 engine's a_above/b_above), AND the sign of (arm - RandomDAG) MRR at the final checkpoint holds in every depth stratum with n >= 500. This is the answer to Burkhard: the model predicts relations it never saw, on a taxonomy it could not have memorised the shape of alone (RandomDAG shares that shape). Overall verdict is GENERALISES only if BOTH vis00 and vis50 reach it independently.
readings.MEMORISES: An arm's per-run MRR sits at or is not meaningfully separated from the floor (fails the >=2x-SD margin above chance), OR the arm is statistically indistinguishable from the RandomDAG control (seed ranges overlap, or |mean difference| is inside an equivalence band of max(0.01, 2x pooled seed SD)). Figure 4-class structure is then in-sample only; the manuscript must say so rather than claim generalisation.
readings.MIXED: The sign of (arm - RandomDAG) flips across depth strata, or the two real-tree arms (vis00, vis50) reach different readings from each other. Reported per stratum and per arm; no single aggregate claim is made.
readings.UNINFORMATIVE: Any of gates (a)/(b)/(c) fails for any seed of any arm, including RandomDAG. A failed gate always wins over every other reading, same as the Task 8/9 engine -- never read a direction out of an invalid run.

p2_amendment_1_20260924.status: WRITTEN AFTER task-7-report.md's freeze (commit 015b8a7), 2026-09-24 -- BEFORE any P2 array was submitted and BEFORE any P2 outcome data (a real checkpoint, a real MRR, a real normalized_rank, for any arm, any seed) had been observed. Stated plainly because that is the material fact a reader needs: this amendment could in principle be outcome-driven, and the defence is that it is not -- the defect below was derived from the STRUCTURE of the RandomDAG control itself, measurable before any run, not from a result. Revises the CROSS-TREE reading only; the frozen block above is untouched (revise only by adding a dated amendment block, never by editing the frozen one -- same convention as results/recipe_angular_comparison.json's preregistration_v2_amendment_1_20260922/_amendment_2_20260924 and results/objective_integrity_delta_preregistration.json).
p2_amendment_1_20260924.derivation: helpers/p2_randomdag_changes_the_chance_floor.py is a read-only measurement over the mollusca_6447_clean closure (seed 0) that exists independently of any P2 training run: it calls randomdag.randomize_parents directly on the real closure and compares fan-out and sibling_chance before vs after rewiring. No embedding, no checkpoint, no trained model was involved in producing the table below.
p2_amendment_1_20260924.what_it_changes: The CROSS-TREE comparison only -- an arm (vis00 or vis50, scored against the real taxonomy) vs the RandomDAG control (scored against a randomised taxonomy). An arm's OWN validity gates (a/b/c, all on its own tree) and its own floor margin (own MRR vs its own baselines.sibling_chance_mean) are UNCHANGED -- those are within-tree and unaffected by this defect. vis00-vs-vis50 is also UNCHANGED -- both real-tree, same pools, MRR remains comparable there.
the_defect: randomdag.randomize_parents draws each non-root node's new parent uniformly at random from the level above, preserving DEPTH exactly (so the closure pair count -- sum of depths -- is preserved exactly, per its own docstring) but NOT preserving FAN-OUT: a real taxonomy's fan-out is heavy-tailed (a few genera with hundreds of children, most nodes with one or two), so uniform reassignment collapses most randomised grandparents toward 1-2 children.

Measured on mollusca_6447_clean, seed 0: mean fan-out over nodes with >=1 child 4.61 (real tree) vs 1.96 (randomised); max fan-out 187 vs 14; internal nodes 6,946 vs 16,343; leaves 25,071 vs 15,674; band-eligible leaves (depth in [11,28]) 7,405 vs 6,070; mean sibling_chance (1/grandparent fan-out, P2's chance floor) 0.10330 (real) vs 0.55816 (randomised); median sibling_chance 0.0417 vs 0.5000.

Mean chance-floor ratio randomised/real = 5.403. RandomDAG's held-out task is therefore, on average, ~5.4x EASIER at chance than the real-tree task it exists to control for -- a materially DIFFERENT-DIFFICULTY task, not merely a scrambled one.

Consequence for the frozen reading: the readings above compare an arm's raw MRR head-to-head against RandomDAG's raw MRR (all-above-all on MRR; an equivalence band computed on MRR). Because RandomDAG's own chance floor is ~5.4x higher, RandomDAG can out-score (or tie) a real, genuinely-generalising arm on raw MRR almost regardless of what the model learned -- which the frozen rule reads as MEMORISES or MIXED. A false MEMORISES verdict is the single worst outcome this control exists to avoid, since it would be read as refuting Figure 4-class generalisation when the geometry never had the chance to demonstrate it on equal footing.
p2_amendment_1_20260924.declared_confound_5: RandomDAG rewiring preserves each node's DEPTH exactly but not its FAN-OUT: mean chance-floor ratio randomised/real = 5.403 on mollusca_6447_clean seed 0 (see the_defect above, and helpers/p2_randomdag_changes_the_chance_floor.py). RandomDAG is therefore a DIFFERENT-DIFFICULTY task, not merely a scrambled one -- which is why every cross-tree read (an arm vs RandomDAG) is chance-normalised (normalized_rank), never raw MRR, under this amendment.

the_correction.rule_1: Any CROSS-TREE comparison (an arm vs RandomDAG) uses normalized_rank = (rank-1)/(pool-1), never MRR. Under a random ranking, rank is uniform on 1..pool, so E[normalized_rank] = ((pool-1)/2)/(pool-1) = 0.5 for EVERY pool size -- exactly the pool-size (and so fan-out) invariance the real-vs-RandomDAG comparison needs. Lower normalized_rank is better. WITHIN-tree comparisons (vis00 vs vis50; an arm vs its OWN sibling_chance_mean) still use MRR as primary: same tree, same pools, comparable, and untouched by this defect.
the_correction.rule_2: Each arm is read against its OWN chance floor -- already true in the frozen implementation (p2_verdict reads baselines_randomdag.sibling_chance_mean for the control and baselines.sibling_chance_mean for vis00/vis50, via p2_group_stats called once per arm with that arm's own floor). This amendment does not change that; it is restated here because it is the within-tree half of the same principle whose cross-tree half (rule_1) this amendment fixes -- never compare an arm's MRR to the OTHER tree's floor.
the_correction.rule_3: GENERALISES (amended): the arm's own MRR still clears its own sibling_chance_mean by the original margin (>= 2x pooled within-arm seed SD, own-tree, unchanged -- checked on the weakest/minimum seed) AND the arm's normalized_rank sits below every RandomDAG seed's normalized_rank (all-below-all, the direct mirror of the frozen all-above-all-on-MRR condition -- no run of the arm may be at or above any run of the control) AND the arm's normalized_rank is below the pool-size-invariant chance level of 0.5 on its weakest (highest) seed AND the sign of (arm - RandomDAG) normalized_rank is negative in every depth stratum with n>=500. MEMORISES (amended): the arm fails its own MRR margin, OR its normalized_rank is statistically indistinguishable from RandomDAG's normalized_rank (seed ranges overlap, or |mean difference| < max(0.01, 2x pooled seed SD), all computed on normalized_rank). MIXED (amended): the sign of (arm - RandomDAG) normalized_rank flips across depth strata, or vis00 and vis50 reach different readings from each other (unchanged from the frozen rule).

p2_amendment_2_20260924.status: WRITTEN 2026-09-24, BEFORE any P2 array was submitted and BEFORE any P2 outcome data (a real checkpoint, a real MRR, a real normalized_rank, for any arm, any seed) had been observed. This amendment follows a USER DESIGN decision about the ARM STRUCTURE, not an observed result -- the user chose to run the RandomDAG control at both visibility settings so that every real arm has a matched control, before any P2 array existed to read a result from. It is additive only: the frozen block above and p2_amendment_1_20260924 are both left completely intact -- revise only by adding a dated amendment block, never by editing a prior one.
p2_amendment_2_20260924.why: A control is only clean against an arm trained the same way. The frozen design trained RandomDAG once, at visibility 0.0, and read BOTH vis00 and vis50 against that single control. That is a fair control for vis00 (same visibility, same number of optimizer steps taking ancestry rows into account) but a CONFOUNDED one for vis50: comparing vis50 (trained with 50% of depth_diff>=2 rows visible) against a RandomDAG control trained at 0% visibility mixes two things the comparison cannot separate -- 'does the model generalise beyond the scrambled shape' and 'does more visible ancestry during training change the score', i.e. the visibility knob leaks into what is supposed to be a pure real-vs-scrambled contrast. The fix is to run RandomDAG at both visibilities too, so each real arm is read against a control trained under its OWN visibility setting and nothing else differs between an arm and its control except real-vs-randomised taxonomy.

p2_amendment_2_20260924.test: tests/eval/test_preregistration.py::TestP2Amendment2::test_cross_matching_the_controls_changes_the_verdict is the load-bearing test: it builds a 12-arm fixture where randomdag_vis00 is a weak control and randomdag_vis50 is a strong one (close to vis50's own score), then swaps which label the two controls' checkpoint data sit under and re-reads the verdict. If the matched pairing were decorative (a verdict that would be the same however the controls were assigned to arms), this test would show no difference and therefore fails to prove the amendment does anything; the pairing being load-bearing means the swap must change vis50's reading.
